title: Separate expression construction, coercion and evaluation
brief: expr_fn helpers and ScalarUDF::call construct expressions. Ordinary analysis supplies type coercion; a direct simplifier call has type preconditions and may leave an incompatible expression unsimplified or fail.

choices.tradeoff: Uses the session analyzer/planner pipeline; still inspect inferred output fields.
Provide the correct DFSchema and SimplifyContext; not every incompatible pair has a coercion.
ColumnarValue may be scalar or array; field/type/length context matters.

claims.statement: ScalarUDF::call(Vec<Expr>) -> Expr does not promise validation or casts. ExprSchemable can infer type/nullability against a schema; it is not execution.
simplify expects types compatible with operator requirements. coerce(expr, schema) -> Result<Expr> is separate. An uncoerced call need not always error; it may remain unsimplified.
Use planning context and registry appropriate to the query. Failures can occur during coercion, physical planning or evaluation; test all relevant boundaries.

implementation: Identify whether the caller enters normal analysis or bypasses it.
For direct processing, coerce with the intended schema, then simplify and plan.
Check both output datatype and value; include an unsupported pair control.
unknowns: Mixed integer addition is the runtime example; it is not a complete coercion matrix.

evidence.scope: Pinned hosted rustdoc; availability depends on the consumer profile.
Only the named assertions in the recorded Cargo profile.

invalidation.reason: Review changed signatures, docs, availability, and newly viable alternatives.
